MEMORANDUM (PRIVILEGED / ATTORNEY WORK PRODUCT)
To: Craig Halloran | Re: Prismex Analytics / Dr. Ananya Mehrotra - PERM A-18247-63910 vs. credentials; H-1B/I-129 readiness | Posture: as of Melanie Foss's June 4, 2025 email (confirm what has happened since)

1. BOTTOM LINE
(a) The certified PERM cannot safely support an I-140 as filed. J.B.5 requires "AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty certification or equivalent." Dr. Mehrotra does not hold it (counsel's own certification compilation confirms this), yet ETA 9089 K.3 and K.4 answer "Yes." This is a material, probably incurable gap and a candor problem.
(b) Education and the 5-year experience requirement are met on the documents, with cleanup items.
(c) The H-1B petition does not depend on the PERM. HR's premise ("certified PERM, so we're good to file the I-129") is wrong. The H-1B needs a certified LCA and specialty-occupation/qualification showings, which she satisfies through her U.S. M.S. in Computer Science.
(d) Urgent: the FY2026 cap filing window ended June 30, 2025 (confirm on the selection notice), not July 15. Filing by July 15 would forfeit the selection and the cap-gap.

2. REQUIREMENT-BY-REQUIREMENT MATRIX (PERM Sec. J.B vs. evidence)
Education - Master's in CS, ML or closely related field. MET. NC State transcript: M.S. Computer Science conferred May 12, 2018, GPA 3.74, thesis approved April 27, 2018. The IAE evaluation (Feb. 15, 2025) covers only the B.Tech in Electronics and Communication Engineering and is unnecessary for this requirement because the M.S. is a U.S. degree. Note IAE itself says the B.Tech has only about 12-15 computer credits, so do not rely on the B.Tech for any "related field" argument.

Experience - 5 years progressive post-master's experience in ML engineering or closely related occupation. MET, with caveats. Only DataBridge counts (June 4, 2018 to filing March 15, 2025 is about 6 years 9 months; Data Scientist I to II promotion supports "progressive"). Evalpoint (2013-2016) and the NC State RA (2016-2018, 20 hrs/week) pre-date the master's and cannot count, and Evalpoint's letter describes ML exposure as "ancillary" and "basic." Caveats: (i) K.2 says "approximately 7 years"; the accurate figure at filing is about 6.75 years. (ii) The experience clock must be satisfied as of the filing date, not later. (iii) All letters in the file show blank signature lines ("By: ____"); obtain signed originals on letterhead. (iv) Confirm the DataBridge role is "ML engineering or closely related" (the letter says "machine learning model development"; reasonable, and consistent with the SOC 15-2051 PWD).

Special skills:
(a) Production deep-learning with TensorFlow or PyTorch - SUPPORTED. DataBridge letter: TensorFlow from 2018, TensorFlow and PyTorch from 2021; SageMaker "production-grade" endpoints. The letter never uses "production-grade" for model design itself; minor.
(b) Apache Spark - SUPPORTED, from Jan. 2021 (Spark MLlib). About 4.2 years at filing.
(c) NLP pipelines - SUPPORTED (clinical NLP, NER, sentiment).
(d) AWS SageMaker or Vertex AI - SUPPORTED from 2021 (EC2 before). 
(e) "Proficiency in Python and R" - WEAK. Python is solid. R is "some use of R for statistical reporting and ad hoc data analysis" (letter) and "R (intermediate)" (resume), plus one NC State R course. Proficiency is not stated by the supervisor. Obtain a supplemental letter or project evidence of R work, if truthful.
Interpretation risk: (b), (d) and PyTorch were gained only since 2021 (about 4.2 years), so a reading that all 5 years must include each skill would fail. The better reading is that the 5 years in the field must "include" these skills somewhere; USCIS applies the plain language of the certification, not the employer's unstated intent (Matter of Wing's Tea House, 16 I&N Dec. 158 (Act. Reg'l Comm'r 1977); Madany v. Smith, 696 F.2d 1008 (D.C. Cir. 1983); Rosedale Linden Park Co. v. Smith, 595 F. Supp. 829 (D.D.C. 1984)). Ambiguity is construed against the party seeking the benefit in practice, so treat this as moderate risk.

AWS Certified Machine Learning - Specialty "or equivalent" - NOT MET.
- Dr. Mehrotra confirmed she holds no ML-Specialty or other specialty AWS certification.
- AWS Cloud Practitioner is foundational (not ML) and EXPIRED January 18, 2025, before the March 15, 2025 filing; it is not equivalent and was not even current.
- TensorFlow Developer Certificate (Google, active) is framework-specific, vendor-different, and tests model-building, not AWS ML architecture/deployment. At best it supports an "equivalent" argument; it is a weak one. The 9089 does not define "equivalent," and no equivalent was stated in recruitment.
- Qualification is measured at the priority date (filing date): Matter of Katigbak, 14 I&N Dec. 45 (Reg'l Comm'r 1971). Passing the AWS exam now does not cure it, and a certified 9089 cannot be amended. 
- Consequences: USCIS will deny an I-140 where the beneficiary lacks a stated requirement (Wing's Tea House; Madany). More seriously, K.3/K.4 "Yes" answers signed by the employer and alien under penalty of perjury risk a misrepresentation finding: DOL may invalidate a certification for fraud or willful misrepresentation (20 CFR 656.30(d)), and 20 CFR 656.31 and 18 U.S.C. 1546 are implicated. I could not retrieve the regulation text during research; verify 656.30 and 656.31 before relying on them.
- Also, U.S. applicants were rejected for education/experience; if the employer would hire without the certification it is not a bona fide minimum requirement (20 CFR 656.17(h)), and if it was a real requirement, any applicant lacking it was properly rejected, but the foreign worker fails the same test (656.24(b)(2)).
Supervisory duty (3-5 ML engineers) - she supervised 2 junior data scientists. This is a job duty, not an experience requirement in J.B.3, so it is not a disqualifier, but note the mismatch and be careful in any future filing.

3. OTHER INCONSISTENCIES IN THE PACKAGE
1. FEIN mismatch: 9089 C.7 shows 84-3291756; the PWD shows 84-3291047. Verify against IRS records; one is wrong. This must be fixed before any I-140/I-129/LCA relies on either document.
2. Employment-authorization chronology: She graduated May 2018 and has worked at DataBridge since June 4, 2018, yet is described as on STEM OPT expiring September 15, 2025. Initial OPT (12 months) plus one STEM extension (24 months) would have ended around mid-2021 on a May 2018 degree. Something is missing (an earlier H-1B, a second degree, a different status, a gap). Obtain her full I-20, EAD, I-94 and status history now. This affects the cap-gap analysis, the validity of 'experience' representations, and the I-94 (the number format and its "2023" prefix also look anomalous).
3. Recruitment report points to check before any reliance: the worksite notice is described as "December 1, 2024 - January 1, 2025 (30 consecutive business days)," but that span contains only about 21 business days, and the notice of filing (20 CFR 656.10(d)) requires 10 consecutive business days; confirm the actual dates. It is listed under "additional" steps; confirm the mandatory Notice of Filing and the three additional steps were correctly counted (campus recruitment is allowed only because a degree is required). Only one additional step may fall within 30 days of filing (website posting ran to Feb. 28, 2025; filing Mar. 15). Get the full recruitment file from Broadleaf and make sure counsel was not involved in screening (656.10(b)(2)).
4. Wage level: PWD is Level III for master's plus 5 years. Supervision of 3-5 staff and a specialty certification can raise the level under DOL's 2009 guidance; confirm the PWD request disclosed the same requirements as the 9089.
5. Resume vs. letters: resume adds details not in the DataBridge letter (50 million encounter records, A/B testing, Docker, Airflow) and says "peer-reviewed conference papers" for workshop papers. Resume should not go beyond what supervisors verify. The resume's "7+ years" summary should be reconciled.
6. RA verification: the missing NC State letter is NOT a gap for the 5-year requirement because RA work is pre-master's. The transcript already documents the appointment (Aug. 15, 2016 - May 15, 2018, NSF IIS-1742956, supervisor Prof. Tsai). Low priority; a department administrator or Graduate School letter would be a nice-to-have if the RA entry stays on the form.

4. H-1B (I-129) AND CAP-GAP QUESTIONS
- H-1B basis: a certified LCA (ETA-9035) for Austin MSA at not less than the higher of actual or prevailing wage ($142,000 offered vs. $131,747 PWD, so fine), plus specialty occupation and qualification (8 CFR 214.2(h)(4)(iii)). The U.S. M.S. in Computer Science qualifies. Do not submit the PERM or its certification claims as H-1B evidence, and ensure the I-129 job description, SOC code, duties and minimum requirements are consistent with, and not broader than, anything already attested; inconsistent statements across filings are a credibility risk.
- Filing window: selection notices state April 1 to June 30, 2025. A July 15 target is outside the window. File immediately; if the window has passed, escalate (a late petition is ordinarily denied and the cap-gap is lost).
- Cap-gap: Under 8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi) as amended by the H-1B Modernization rule (effective Jan. 17, 2025), a timely filed cap-subject change-of-status petition with an Oct. 1 start date automatically extends F-1 status and OPT work authorization until April 1, 2026 (or earlier rejection/denial/approval start date), not October 1. It is not "automatic" in the sense of requiring no action: the petition must be properly filed (receipt notice) while she is in a valid F-1 status/OPT period and request change of status, not consular notification. Her DSO must update SEVIS. She can continue working for DataBridge during cap-gap but the Austin move and Prismex employment cannot start until H-1B approval and the October 1 start. Confirm the exact regulatory text and current USCIS guidance; I could not access the primary sources and relied on secondary summaries.

5. REMEDIAL RECOMMENDATIONS (priority order)
1. This week: file the I-129 within the cap window with LCA and a clean, PERM-independent record. Resolve the FEIN mismatch first.
2. Obtain her full immigration chronology to explain the OPT dates.
3. Do NOT file an I-140 on A-18247-63910 until the certification issue is resolved. The 180-day I-140 filing deadline from certification (20 CFR 656.30(b); May 22, 2025 certification points to about November 18, 2025) is not a reason to file a petition we believe is unsupportable.
4. Ask the employer (Mr. Sunderajan) whether the AWS ML-Specialty requirement was ever the actual minimum, and why K.3 was answered "Yes." Document the answer. Evaluate whether this firm prepared the form; counsel (Texas bar) has duties of candor (Tex. Disciplinary R. Prof'l Conduct 3.03; 8 CFR 292.3 / 1003.102 for immigration practice). Consider conflict/ethics review and advising the employer and beneficiary of the separate exposure; the beneficiary signed under penalty of perjury and may need independent advice.
5. Options for the green card, best to worst: (A) New PERM with accurate requirements (delete the certification, or state "or equivalent experience"), with new recruitment and PWD review; priority date resets. (B) Dr. Mehrotra sits for AWS ML-Specialty, then file a new PERM listing it as met; a new PERM is needed either way. (C) Argue "or equivalent" using TensorFlow cert plus 4+ years of SageMaker/ML production experience; high risk, and does not address the sworn "Yes" answers. (D) Voluntary withdrawal or non-use of the certification; do not file the I-140 and do not make misstatements to USCIS if asked. Do not attempt to amend the certified form.
6. For the supplemental evidence: signed DataBridge letter that confirms R proficiency and production deployment, and corrects the date to January 3/4, 2021; signed Evalpoint letter; optional NC State administrative letter. Revise the resume to conform to the verified letters.
7. Respond to HR: explain the PERM/H-1B distinction, the June 30 deadline, cap-gap (April 1), and request the missing documents (I-20/EAD/SEVIS history, FEIN confirmation, full recruitment file, selection notice, payroll/ability-to-pay proof if requested).

6. OPEN POINTS
- Primary regulations (8 CFR 214.2(f)(5)(vi); 20 CFR 656.30, 656.31, 656.17) and the selection notice were not retrieved directly (sources blocked); verified only via secondary summaries and my knowledge. Cite-check before sending.
- Whether Dr. Mehrotra's non-possession of the certificate was known to the preparer on March 14, 2025.
